title: Test, debug, and publish static site
learningObjectives: Complete test, debug, and publish static site using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: A static-site release should validate file paths, links, HTML/CSS/JavaScript behaviour, responsive layout, accessibility, and hosting configuration. Deployment should run from a known commit and include a post-deploy smoke test and rollback plan.
understand.whyItMatters: A page that works locally may fail when hosted because of paths, routing, caching, MIME types, or environment configuration. Release checks catch these differences.
understand.analogy: Publishing is opening the site to visitors after the final inspection, with a safe path back if something breaks.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The checklist identifies common release checks. A real release needs evidence from the actual hosted site.

examples.code: const checks=['Links resolve','Console has no unexpected errors','Assets load','Keyboard flow works','Responsive checks pass','HTTPS and routes work'];console.log(checks);
examples.explanation: The checklist identifies common release checks. A real release needs evidence from the actual hosted site.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Deploy the static project to a test host. Verify routes, assets, HTTPS, console, and a core user task before sharing the URL.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
